slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise 2027 renewal prices 10% in mid-market, 7% in enterprise and 8% in other SMB, and hold the 2025 promotion cohort while it is onboarded
Churn is rising because of customers the 2025 SMB promotion brought in
–	SMB holds 80% of customers but only 24% of ARR, and only its churn jumped
–	The promotion cohort is 36% of SMB customers but 56% of those who leave
Customers outside the promotion can take a rise; SMB carries the most Inkwell risk
–	Mid-market and enterprise hold 76% of ARR and keep 112% and 118% of revenue
–	Inkwell's $9 plan cut SMB win rates from 51% to 38%; other SMB churn barely moved
The CFO's 12% is worth $7.6M, not $10.3M; a segmented rise adds $5.5M before churn
–	Only $65.5M of ARR renews in 2027, and 60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7%
–	Each step rests on a test, a precedent or a cap; the promotion cohort is held
–	The 15% target is reached only if existing customers keep today's 109% retention
Reprice from January with an SMB control group, onboard the cohort, stop if churn spikes
–	Mid-market 10%, enterprise 7%, other SMB 8%; no rise for the promotion cohort
–	A March read-out stops the SMB rise if churn runs above the 2023 reaction

slides.title: Onboarding the promotion cohort could keep up to $1.0M of ARR a year, but it cannot halve SMB churn

paragraphs.text: 1 Churn    2 Pricing power    3 Options    4 Plan
Onboarding the promotion cohort could keep up to $1.0M of ARR a year, but it cannot halve SMB churn
ARR kept by onboarding the promotion cohort, $ millions, first 12 months, upper bound
ARR in the promotion cohort today, at full price
more of it kept after 12 months at other SMB churn: 77.5% compared with 54.7%
ARR kept in a year, at most, before programme cost
The ceiling assumes full activation; the evidence supports less
▪	Ceiling: the cohort's churn falls from 4.9% a month to the 2.1% of other SMB customers from January
▪	Activation explains only part of the gap: low users churn about three times as fast, so 41% activation predicts 2.9%, not 4.9%
▪	If the rest is a lasting reaction to the discount ending, full activation cuts churn to 3.3% and keeps about $0.5M
▪	Halving SMB churn, as proposed, means 1.55% a month, below the 2.1% of SMB customers the promotion never touched
▪	The briefing pack gives no programme cost; logo churn is applied to the cohort's ARR
1  Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; live formulas are in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook
Sources: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis
